cues.text: Here's Alice's little world, and its shelf. A shelf is just a pair: some data, and then its version, which has a version number for every piece of the data.
And here's Bob, with a second copy of the same world, and its own shelf.
We want to keep them in sync.
Say Alice wants to change the lamp's color. In code, that's one call to shelf_merge, with just the part she changed.
The shelf writes down the new color, and bumps its version, from 1 to 2.
Then it packs up just what changed: the new color with its version, plus the path to get there.
That little package goes over to Bob.
There, the same call merges it in. It compares versions, from the top. Same version? Look inside.
For the color, 2 beats 1, so the new color wins.
For the color, 2 beats 1, so the new color wins.
